body:
`helper.get_book_cover_with_uuid` (cps/helper.py) and `helper.get_kobo_cover_source_path`
resolve the book with `calibre_db.get_book_by_uuid`, which applies NO filter (cps/db.py) —
unlike the numbered `/cover/<id>` route, which goes through `get_filtered_book` and therefore
`common_filters`. `cps/kobo.py`'s cover handler uses the same raw lookup.

A policy-aware alternative already exists and is used elsewhere:
`get_book_by_uuid_for_kobo(..., enforce_policy=True)` (cps/db.py).

So a Kobo cover request naming another user's restricted book's UUID is answered from that
book rather than refused. Pre-existing; found by an adversarial review of PR #1739 (which
asked explicitly whether its new cache policy could attach to "a different user's book" — the
caching change does not reach this path, but the underlying lookup does).

Smallest fix: use the policy-aware lookup in both UUID cover helpers.
title: Kobo cover lookup by UUID bypasses per-user visibility filtering

resolution.note: Fixed by #1947 (My Library). Verified on main 1b5417a2a by reading the call sites, not by trusting the merge: helper.get_book_cover_with_uuid and helper.get_kobo_cover_source_path both now resolve via get_book_by_uuid_for_kobo(..., enforce_policy=True), and kobo.py's cover handler reaches the policy-aware lookup THROUGH those two helpers rather than calling it directly. NOT every book lookup was rerouted: three deliberate enforce_policy=False call sites remain - shelf removal, reading-state GET/PUT, and book deletion - which are unfiltered on purpose per notes/KOBO-B4-COMMON-FILTERS-POLICY.md so a device can always clean up books it already holds. IT WAS FIXED BUT UNGUARDED: TestNoLegacyBypass audits cps/kobo.py only, and both cover helpers live in cps/helper.py, so reverting either line reintroduced the bug with a fully green suite. Closed with two guards: a source guard pinning both helpers, and an EXECUTING test that invokes each helper against a mocked lookup and asserts the uuid and enforce_policy=True actually passed - because a source assertion stays green against a regression that keeps the call and discards its result. Mutation-tested: raw-lookup revert, polarity flip, and result-discarded, all red.
